definition: Conditioning on the ground-truth prefix rather than the model's own during training, and across 3 sources both a training convention and a measurement device. As a convention it is what creates the train-inference mismatch on-policy methods exist to remove. As a measurement it is used well: a process reward computed as the increase in a frozen reference policy's teacher-forced likelihood of a gold translation, so a step that makes the reference more predictable is rewarded. And as a theoretical object one source proves that chain-of-thought learning under it costs only logarithmically more in sample complexity as the number of reasoning steps grows, which is the formal reason the convention is affordable.

evidence.note: Scores each reasoning step of a translation by how much appending it raises a frozen reference model's teacher-forced likelihood of the gold translation, and adds that as a dense per-step reward on top of sequence-level quality — after first establishing that explicit reasoning helps long and hard inputs while drifting on terminology and style.
evidence.title: PAMT: Process-Aligned Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Domain Machine Translation

evidence.note: Adds a higher-level abstract latent as an auxiliary pretraining target to reduce compounding error in latent-space rollouts, aiming at longer-horizon coherence than multi-token or next-latent prediction.
evidence.title: Hierarchical Latent Prediction for Language Models

evidence.note: Pins down the VC dimension of transformers as depth times parameters times a logarithm, and shows chain-of-thought learning by teacher forcing costs only logarithmically more as the number of reasoning steps grows.
evidence.title: Tight Sample Complexity of Transformers

name: teacher forcing
